key_insight: Medical world models aim to move medical AI from static prediction to simulating how patient states change over time and how different interventions may alter those futures.
clinical_relevance: If successful, these systems could help clinicians anticipate deterioration, compare treatment scenarios, and personalize care based on likely disease trajectories.
method: Build patient-state representations from longitudinal and foundation-model data
Model clinical dynamics as an internal simulator of disease progression
Support intervention planning via treatment-conditioned rollouts, treatment-effect estimation, RL, or digital-twin-style systems
evidence_signal: This is a review paper synthesizing representative systems across foundation models, longitudinal modeling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins rather than reporting a single new clinical dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: Plausible simulated rollouts may still be clinically misleading unless they are rigorously validated, interpretable, and robust across diverse patient populations and settings.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
